358344.title: Conjecture that fewer graphs lie in A than in B
358344.statement:
Let ${\mathcal G}_n$ be the set of graphs of order $n$. For a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, let $M_1(G)$ and $M_2(G)$ denote its first and second Zagreb indices, respectively. Define

$$
A=\left\{G\in{\mathcal G}_n:\frac{M_1(G)}{n}>\frac{M_2(G)}{m}\right\},\qquad
B=\left\{G\in{\mathcal G}_n:\frac{M_1(G)}{n}=\frac{M_2(G)}{m}\right\}.
$$

**The $A$–$B$ cardinality conjecture.** $|A|<|B|$.

The paper presents this as a relevant conjecture after proving that, for $n>3$, the class $C$ of graphs satisfying $M_1(G)/n<M_2(G)/m$ has greater cardinality than both $A$ and $B$. The conjecture itself is not resolved in the supplied text.
358344.source_name: Batmend Horoldagva and Kinkar Chandra Das, “On Zagreb indices of graphs”, arXiv:2305.05878 (2023).
358344.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05878

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2023). “Although this conjecture is disproved for general graphs , it was the beginning of a long series of studies to characterize the graphs $G$ for which $G\in A$ or $G\in B$ or $G\in C$, see and the references cited therein.”

358557.title: Conjecture on affine Hermitian intersections with curves of Frobenius type
358557.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $h\geq 2$, and set $q=p^{2h}$. In the affine plane $\mathrm{AG}(2,q^2)$, consider the affine Hermitian curve $\mathcal H(q^2)$ and the curves

$$
\mathcal X(a,m,d)\colon y=ax^p+mx+d.
$$

Here $a,m,d\in\mathrm{GF}(q^2)$, with the parameters subject to the definition of the curves $\mathcal X(a,m,d)$. **Affine Hermitian intersection conjecture.** The affine Hermitian curve $\mathcal H(q^2)$ meets each curve $\mathcal X(a,m,d)$ in a number of affine points congruent to $1$ modulo $p$. This conjecture proposes a uniform congruence for these intersection numbers in the generalized setting $q=p^{2h}$, extending the preceding analysis of intersections with curves of the corresponding affine type.
358557.source_name: Angela Aguglia, Bence Csajbók and Luca Giuzzi, “On regular sets of affine type in finite Desarguesian planes and related codes”, arXiv:2305.17103 (2023).
358557.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17103

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

358589.title: The maximal clustering word conjecture for Arnoux–Rauzy languages
358589.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be an Arnoux–Rauzy language satisfying condition $(Rabc)$. A **clustering word** is a word whose occurrences cluster in the sense defined for $\Lambda$, and a word is **conjugate to a standard Arnoux–Rauzy word** if it is a cyclic conjugate of such a word. Let $w$ denote the word constructed in Proposition. **Maximal clustering word conjecture.** The word $w$ is the longest clustering word in $\Lambda$; if this is false, then $w$ is the longest clustering word conjugate to a standard Arnoux–Rauzy word. The conjecture concerns the sharpness of the bound for clustering words in Arnoux–Rauzy languages; the examples preceding the statement indicate that the proposed word can be maximal, although uniqueness and maximality depend on the directive word.
358589.source_name: Sébastien Ferenczi and Luca Q. Zamboni, “Clustering and Arnoux-Rauzy words”, arXiv:2305.18986 (2023).
358589.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18986

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

358590.title: Genericity conjecture for g-rigidity matroids and sparsity matroids
358590.statement:
Let $g:(\mathbb{F}^d)^k\to\mathbb{F}$ be a polynomial map, let ${\cal M}_{g,n}$ be its $g$-rigidity matroid on the $k$-uniform complete hypergraph, and let ${\cal S}_n^{d,0}$ be the $(d,0)$-sparsity matroid. **Genericity conjecture.** If $g$ is generic, then

$$
{\cal M}_{g,n}={\cal S}_n^{d,0}.
$$

The conjecture asks whether the combinatorial upper bound for the rank of the $g$-rigidity matroid is always attained for sufficiently generic polynomial maps. It extends the Geiringer–Laman phenomenon beyond the squared-distance setting, while the surrounding discussion notes that strict inequality occurs for many naturally arising nongeneric examples.
358590.source_name: James Cruickshank, Fatemeh Mohammadi, Anthony Nixon and Shin-ichi Tanigawa, “Identifiability of Points and Rigidity of Hypergraphs under Algebraic Constraints”, arXiv:2305.18990 (2024).
358590.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18990

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2023). “It is an open problem to analyse global $g$-rigidity in the $\ell_p$ case.”

358615.title: Condensation and densification conjecture for Vinogradov mean values
358615.statement:
Let ${\mathscr A}\subset {\mathbb Z}$ be finite, let $A=|{\mathscr A}|$, and let $s,k\in{\mathbb N}$. Write $J_{s,k}({\mathscr A})$ for the number of solutions in elements of ${\mathscr A}$ to the corresponding Vinogradov system of equations.

**Condensation and densification conjecture.** One has

$$
J_{s,k}({\mathscr A})\leqslant J_{s,k}(\{1,2,\ldots,A\}.
$$

Moreover, for each $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
J_{s,k}({\mathscr A})\ll_{\varepsilon,s,k} A^{s+\varepsilon}+A^{2s-k(k+1)/2}.
$$

The claim says that, among finite sets of integers of a given cardinality, the initial interval is extremal for the Vinogradov mean value, and that the resulting bound removes the dependence on the diameter of the set. Its status is not determined by the supplied material.
358615.source_name: Trevor D. Wooley, “Condensation and densification for sets of large diameter”, arXiv:2305.19968 (2023).
358615.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19968

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

358638.title: Burns-space scattering amplitudes and defect-free chiral-algebra correlators
358638.statement: Let WZW$_4$ plus Mabuchi gravity be the bulk theory on Burns space, and let the large $N$ chiral algebra be the chiral algebra obtained from the compactification $\overline{\operatorname{SL}}_2(\mathbb{C})$, with no defects and uniquely defined correlators. **Burns-space/chiral-algebra correspondence conjecture.** At all orders in $1/N$, the scattering amplitudes of WZW$_4$ plus Mabuchi gravity on Burns space coincide with the uniquely defined correlators of the large $N$ chiral algebra with no defects. This consequence is derived in the paper from the loop-level equality of holographic correlators and the Penrose transform; its validity therefore remains contingent on that open conjecture.
358638.source_name: Kevin Costello, Natalie M. Paquette and Atul Sharma, “Burns space and holography”, arXiv:2306.00940 (2023).
358638.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00940

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

358642.title: The non-geodesicity conjecture for metric spaces of Reeb graphs
358642.statement:
Let $d$ be any metric on the space of isomorphism classes of Reeb graphs. A metric space is **geodesic** if every pair of points can be joined by a path whose length equals their distance.

**Non-geodesicity conjecture.** The space of isomorphism classes of Reeb graphs with metric $d$ is not a geodesic space.

This generalizes the preceding conjecture that the intrinsic version $\hat{d}_I$ is not strictly intrinsic. The preceding examples show that the interleaving-distance space and the contour-tree space are not geodesic for $d_I$, but the supplied text gives no resolution of the general claim.
358642.source_name: Fangfei Lan, Salman Parsa and Bei Wang, “Labeled Interleaving Distance for Reeb Graphs”, arXiv:2306.01186 (2023).
358642.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.01186

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

358986.title: The permutation-representation conjecture for comparability graphs
358986.statement:
Let $G$ be a **comparability graph**, meaning the graph of a partial order. Write $\mathcal{R}_2$ for the class of graphs with representation number at most two, and $\mathcal{R}^p_{\le 3}$ for the class of graphs with permutation-representation number at most three. **Permutation-representation conjecture.** If

$$
G\in\mathcal{R}_2,
$$

then

$$
G\in\mathcal{R}^p_{\le 3}.
$$

This conjecture proposes that every comparability graph with representation number at most two has permutation-representation number at most three. It is presented as an observation-based conjecture in the paper; no resolution is supplied here.
358986.source_name: Khyodeno Mozhui and K. V. Krishna, “Words for the Graphs with Permutation-Representation Number at most Three”, arXiv:2307.00301 (2023).
358986.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00301

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

359109.title: The refined Forking Path Conjecture for the longest element
359109.statement:
Let $w_{0,n}\in S_n$ be the longest element, let $\Gamma_{w_{0,n}}$ be its conflated expression graph, and let $\mathbf{s}$ and $\mathbf{t}$ be the source and sink of the Manin–Schechtman orientation. For a path $p$, write $p_a$ and $p_z$ for its starting and ending vertices, and let $f(p)$ denote its induced morphism.

**Refined Forking Path Conjecture.** If $p$ and $q$ are paths in $\Gamma_{w_{0,n}}$ that both pass through $\mathbf{s}$ and $\mathbf{t}$, with $p_a=q_a$ and $p_z=q_z$, then

$$
f(p)=f(q).
$$

This is proposed as a strengthening of the Forking Path Conjecture for the longest element. The paper reports that the phenomenon was proved for $S_4$, but does not establish it for the longest element in every $S_n$; its general status is open.
359109.source_name: Gonzalo Jiménez, “On the Forking Path Conjecture”, arXiv:2307.05835 (2023).
359109.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05835

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

359130.title: Reversed Dickson second-kind permutation classification for primes greater than seven
359130.statement:
Let $p>7$ be a prime, and let $E_n(1,x)$ denote the reversed Dickson polynomial of the second kind. A permutation polynomial (PP) is a polynomial that permutes $\mathbb{F}_p$. **The large-prime reversed Dickson permutation conjecture.** $E_n(1,x)$ is a PP of $\mathbb{F}_p$ if and only if

$$
n\equiv 2,3\pmod{p(p^2-1)}.
$$

This extends the explicitly conjectured classifications for $p=5$ and $p=7$; the general classification for $p>7$ is not proved in the source.
359130.source_name: Jiaqi Fang, Neranga Fernando and Haoming Wu, “Reversed Dickson polynomials”, arXiv:2307.06325 (2023).
359130.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.06325

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

359149.title: Girth constraints for diameter-maximal regular graphs
359149.statement:
Let $G$ be a diameter-maximal regular graph, with diameter $D$ and girth $g$.

**Diameter-maximal girth conjecture.** If $D$ is odd, then

$$
g=D+1.
$$

If $D$ is even, then

$$
g\in\{D,D+1,D+2\}.
$$

This conjecture is suggested by the authors' search for diameter-maximal graphs, including examples for degree $3$ and diameter at most $9$ and degree $4$ and diameter at most $6$. It is stated as an open problem.
359149.source_name: Geoffrey Exoo, Theodore Kolokolnikov, Jeanette Janssen and Timothy Salamon, “Attainable bounds for algebraic connectivity and maximally-connected regular graphs”, arXiv:2307.07308 (2023).
359149.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07308

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2023). “We state this as an open problem.”

359310.title: Rigidity conjecture for geometric nonconvex self-intersecting polyhedra
359310.statement: A **geometric polyhedron** here may be nonconvex and self-intersecting; its faces, dihedral angles, edge lengths, and partially-flat vertices are understood in the sense of the paper. **The nonconvex polyhedron rigidity conjecture.** Every geometric, possibly nonconvex and self-intersecting, polyhedron is uniquely determined by its dihedral angles and edge lengths, if it satisfies that (i) every face is convex and (ii) no vertex is partially flat. The result proved in the paper requires an additional condition excluding collinear triples of vertices. The conjecture proposes removing that auxiliary condition and is described as a challenging long-term goal.
359310.source_name: Yunhi Cho and Seonhwa Kim, “Rigidity of nonconvex polyhedra with respect to edge lengths and dihedral angles”, arXiv:2307.14769 (2023).
359310.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14769

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2023). “While a flexible counterexample for the spherical case has been discovered by J.-M. Schlenker and the local rigidity of the hyperbolic case has been proved by R. Mazzeo and G. Montcouquiol , the conjecture still remains unsol”

359338.title: Equivalence characterization for the tree σE
359338.statement:
Let $E$ be a linearly ordered set, and let $\sigma E$ be the tree of all bounded well-ordered subsets of $E$, ordered by initial segment inclusion. The following conditions are equivalent:

**Equivalence conjecture for $\sigma E$.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(1) Neither }\omega_1\text{ nor }\mathbb Q\text{ as linearly ordered sets are contained in }E;\\
&\text{(2) }\sigma E\text{ is a special tree};\\
&\text{(3) }\sigma E\text{ is a }Q\text{-space};\\
&\text{(4) }\sigma E\text{ is a }\Delta\text{-space}.
\end{aligned}
$$

This proposed equivalence is presented as a provisional result conditional on the conjecture that $\sigma\mathbb Q$ is not a $\Delta$-space. The source does not establish that conjecture, and therefore the equivalence remains open.
359338.source_name: Arkady Leiderman and Paul Szeptycki, “On Δ-spaces”, arXiv:2307.16047 (2023).
359338.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

359353.title: Equivalence of left, partitionable and tensor-action convergence for uniform hypergraphs
359353.statement:
Let $H_n=(V(H_n),E(H_n))$ be a sequence of $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $A(H_n)$ denote the normalized adjacency tensors. Left-convergence is convergence of homomorphism densities, and partitionable convergence is the hypergraph convergence notion defined through branching partitions.

**Convergence-equivalence conjecture.** Left-convergence, partitionable convergence, and action convergence of the $(r-1)$-action of the sequence

$$
\frac{A(H_n)}{|V(H_n)|}
$$

of normalized adjacency tensors are equivalent.

Partitionable convergence is already known in the source to imply left-convergence, while the conjecture asserts equivalence with both left-convergence and the $(r-1)$-action convergence of normalized adjacency tensors.
359353.source_name: Giulio Zucal, “Action convergence of general hypergraphs and tensors”, arXiv:2308.00226 (2025).
359353.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00226

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359379.title: Generic identifiability conjecture for all non-complete graph families
359379.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be any family of non-complete graphs, and let $M_G$ denote the homoscedastic linear structural equation model associated with $G\in\mathcal{G}$. **Generic identifiability conjecture.** The graph parameter $G$ of the family $\{M_G\}_{G\in\mathcal{G}}$ is generically identifiable. The claim would extend the paper's established identifiability results from particular graph families to every family of non-complete graphs. It is stated without a proof or resolution.
359379.source_name: Mathias Drton, Benjamin Hollering and Jun Wu, “Identifiability of Homoscedastic Linear Structural Equation Models using Algebraic Matroids”, arXiv:2308.01821 (2023).
359379.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.01821

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359502.title: The conjecture that d-complete posets are LE-cactus
359502.statement: A **d-complete poset** is a poset in the sense of the standard definition of d-completeness. A poset is **LE-cactus** when the Bender–Knuth involutions acting on its linear extensions satisfy the cactus group relations, including $(t_iq_{jk})^2=1$ for $i+1<j<k$, where $q_{jk}=q_{k-1}q_{k-j}q_{k-1}$ and $q_i=t_1(t_2t_1)\cdots(t_it_{i-1}\cdots t_1)$. **The d-complete poset conjecture.** Every d-complete poset is LE-cactus. The conjecture extends the known LE-cactus families, which include Ferrers posets, shifted Ferrers posets, rooted trees, and other minuscule posets; its resolution is not specified in the supplied source.
359502.source_name: Son Nguyen, “The Cactus Group Property for Ordinal Sums of Disjoint Unions of Chains”, arXiv:2308.07240 (2023).
359502.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07240

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359585.title: The bicircular-matroid basis conciseness conjecture
359585.statement: Let $b(M)$ denote the number of bases of a matroid $M$, and restrict $b$ to bicircular matroids. A counting function is **concise** if every positive integer occurs on an input of size polynomial in the logarithm of that integer. **Bicircular-matroid basis conjecture.** The function $b$ restricted to bicircular matroids is concise. Bicircular matroids give a natural concise presentation for a known $\#\mathrm P$-complete basis-counting problem, but the stronger value-realization bound remains open.
359585.source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Igor Pak, “Computational complexity of counting coincidences”, arXiv:2308.10214 (2024).
359585.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10214

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359588.title: The plane-triangulation almost-completeness conjecture
359588.statement: Let $X=\{p_1,\ldots,p_n\}\subset\mathbb Q^2$ be a set of points in general position, and let $t(X)$ be the number of triangulations of the convex hull of $X$ using all points of $X$. **Plane-triangulation conjecture.** The function $t$ is almost complete, meaning that it takes every positive integer except possibly finitely many values. The function has exponential growth, and the abundance of topological triangulations together with their planar realizability provides supporting evidence, but the conjecture remains open.
359588.source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Igor Pak, “Computational complexity of counting coincidences”, arXiv:2308.10214 (2024).
359588.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10214

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359590.title: The simply connected domino-tiling extension conjecture
359590.statement:
A simply connected region is a domino-tileable region in the setting of the paper whose interior has no holes. Let the domino-tiling counting theorem of the paper be denoted by Theorem 
$$
. **Simply connected domino-tiling conjecture.** Theorem
$$
 holds for simply connected regions. The claim extends the paper's result from regions that may have holes to simply connected regions; the supplied text gives no resolution, so it remains open.
359590.source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Igor Pak, “Computational complexity of counting coincidences”, arXiv:2308.10214 (2024).
359590.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10214

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359599.title: Mohar's pseudo-triangulation cross-cap drawing conjecture
359599.statement: Let $g$ be a positive integer, and let $N_g$ be the non-orientable surface of genus $g$. A **loopless pseudo-triangulation** of $N_g$ is a cellularly embedded loopless multigraph in which every face has degree three. A perfect cross-cap drawing has $g$ cross-caps and every edge intersects each cross-cap at most once. **Mohar's pseudo-triangulation conjecture.** Every loopless pseudo-triangulation of $N_g$ admits a perfect cross-cap drawing. The paper explicitly states that this stronger conjecture is disproved by Schaefer and Štefankovič, so it is not an open problem.
359599.source_name: Niloufar Fuladi, Alfredo Hubard and Arnaud de Mesmay, “Degenerate crossing number and signed reversal distance”, arXiv:2308.10666 (2025).
359599.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10666

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2023).
